title: Grateful Dead Live at Reno Centennial Coliseum on 1982-03-13
lineage: MAC > Nakamichi CR-5A > Edirol FA-66 > Wavelab 2448 > CD-Wave (24bit output) > R8Brain > TLH > FLAC 1644 tagged. Transferred by Andrew F. 08/2015
source: AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XLII (S1) and Hitachi ME-Metal (S2). Set up FOB, recording by Brian Schley.

ai_review.summary: Great audience recording of a solid 1982 show with standout Bertha, It Must Have Been the Roses and a blistering Stranger > Franklin's Tower > Estimated Prophet > Eyes of the World sequence.
ai_review.review: The audience tape is praised as a definite upgrade, offering clear, lively sound that captures the energy of this underrated 1982 performance. Highlights include a strong first‑set Bertha and Roses, plus a second‑set stretch—Stranger > Franklin's Tower > Estimated Prophet > Eyes of the World—that is described as blistering, with especially creative guitar work from Jerry.

ai_rating.rationale: A single detailed 5‑star review emphasizes both excellent musical performance and high‑quality audience recording; limited sample size keeps confidence at medium.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewer calls it a "great audience recording" and an "archive upgrade," indicating clear, well‑balanced sound that captures the concert atmosphere.

standout_songs: It Must Have Been the Roses
Stranger > Franklin's Tower > Estimated Prophet > Eyes of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set features strong Bertha and Roses; second set delivers a blistering sequence with tight transitions, including Space into Truckin' using a Dear Prudence reference to segue into Black Peter.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Poignant vocals and solo on the first set; guitar work described as especially creative during Franklin's Tower and Eyes of the World.
